subject: VPC burst credit approval request — Hearthline deployment
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: VPC burst credit for Hearthline — exec approval needed

Hi Marissa / Kim —

Quick background: Hearthline signed on for a Dedicated + Private (VPC) deployment with a cross-region read-replica for resilience. During discovery their infra/clinical teams flagged two constraints that will materially increase first-quarter token/egress consumption: cross-region KV syncs and burst traffic during scheduled HL7 batches. We modeled the first 90 days and expect a one-time overage exposure of ~ $78k if we invoice at list.

Customer asks: they want a single-line commercial trade (one-time credit) to offset onboarding burst risk so they can move forward with the deployment on our VPC timeline. They are sensitive to a multi-month delay. The SOW is otherwise in good shape and the hubspot deal (HL-4783) is in final legal review.

Ask: I need VP/CFO concurrence to grant a one-time "VPC burst credit" of up to $78,000 (split recommended: $50k onboarding credit + $28k conditional burst buffer). Proposed guardrails below:
- Credit applied as contra-revenue on first invoice, recognized over 90 days for ASC/IFRS purposes
- Credit void if customer requests a change that increases committed throughput before production
- Product to ship with KV caching config recommended by Applied ML (internal note attached)

Attachments: Hearthline-SOW-v1.pdf (SOW draft), estimated-burst-usage-90d.csv (model).

Business rationale: Without the credit they will delay by 6–8 weeks pending an internal budget reprioritization. Delaying risks losing the multi-year commitment (they sign for 2yr commitment + Dedicated pool). Granting the credit reduces churn risk and accelerates the committed ARR start date.

I'll pull compliance on any contractual language they require; legal is queued. If agreed, I will prepare the redlined term and ask for DocuSign flow.

Thanks —
David
David Kim
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: VPC burst credit for Hearthline — exec approval needed

David —

Thanks for the concise summary. I reviewed the modeling and agree the commercial risk of delaying is real; Hearthline is close to legal sign-off and the 2yr commitment is material. Happy to support, with a couple of conditions:

1) Split the credit as you suggested ($50k onboarding / $28k conditional) and document the conditionality in the SOW (clear trigger).
2) Finance (Priyom) needs to sign off on the revenue recognition treatment and confirm we can apply the credit as contra-revenue over 90 days.
3) Legal must add the credit clause and a revert clause if consumption materially exceeds modeled burst by >40% in month 1.

Priyom — can you confirm if the proposed treatment is acceptable from your side?

If Priyom + Kim ok, please route to Markus for CFO signoff (cc him once you prepare the short exec memo).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales, East
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 13:21:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: VPC burst credit for Hearthline — exec approval needed

Thanks team —

This aligns with our risk appetite if we keep the credit time-bound and conditional. A couple quick additions from Commercial:
- Limit total one-time credit exposure per customer portfolio to $100k without direct CFO signoff; this ask falls within that but close to the threshold.
- Prefer we structure as an onboarding incentive (apply up to $50k immediately) + a measured burst buffer (hold $28k in a contingency credit to be applied only if documented overage occurs in month 1 or 2).

David, please prepare a 1-page memo for Markus that includes: deal summary, ARR impact, proposed accounting treatment, and recommended approval language (we can copy into the SOW as an annex). I can sign off at VP level; Markus will make the CFO call on whether to approve in full.

Kimberly Park
VP Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: VPC burst credit for Hearthline — exec approval needed

Kimberly / Marissa / David —

Reviewed the memo and the attached usage model. I approve the one-time VPC burst credit under the conditions below:

1) Credit split as requested: $50,000 applied as onboarding credit on the first invoice; $28,000 held as contingent buffer to be applied only upon documented overage during the first 60 days.
2) Finance (Priyom) will confirm contra-revenue posting and recognition schedule (90 days) before signature. No credit should be applied until the accounting entry is agreed.
3) Legal to include an overage audit right in the SOW annex; if overage exceeds modeled amounts by >40% in month 1, Redwood may invoice the excess or revoke the remaining contingency.
4) This approval is one-time and not precedent setting; Commercial to log the credit in the pricing-exceptions registry with justification.

Once Priyom confirms accounting mechanics, route the SOW to DocuSign. Good to proceed assuming legal and procurement are aligned.

Markus Klein
Chief Financial Officer
Redwood Inference
